name: Racket
note: began as PLT Scheme in 1995 and was renamed Racket in 2010; language-oriented
typeSystem: Dynamic by default (the base #lang racket), with an optional, soundly and statically typed dialect, Typed Racket, that gradually layers static types onto dynamically typed code and modules.
runtime: Racket CS compiles programs to native code through an embedded, heavily modified Chez Scheme backend; Racket is also a 'language-oriented programming' platform where #lang can select an entirely different surface syntax while sharing the same macro-expander and runtime.

runtimes.name: Racket CS (Chez Scheme backend)
runtimes.role: Default modern implementation: compiles to native code via an embedded Chez Scheme.

runtimes.name: Racket BC (legacy bytecode)
runtimes.role: Older 'before Chez' implementation, with its own bytecode format and JIT.

compilers.name: raco make / raco exe
compilers.role: raco make precompiles modules; raco exe packages a program with its runtime dependencies as a standalone executable, but does not by itself imply native machine-code compilation of the program.

concurrencyModel: Coroutine threads provide shared-state concurrency; Racket CS also offers parallel threads and futures. Places are separate Racket instances that communicate primarily through restricted message passing.
